episode_title: Building a New Career After Military Service with Brian McGrath

real_qa.q: What are the three core project management principles Brian McGrath applies as a Senior Project Leader at MCFA?
real_qa.r: Brian focuses on scope, schedule, and budget as the three core pillars he leads and ensures the owner is comfortable with throughout the project. Scope ensures the contract requirements are accurate and fulfill the entire job with no changes. Schedule ensures delivery by the target date or earlier. Budget ensures the project stays at or below the agreed number. He applies these three things consistently across every project type.

real_qa.q: What was Brian McGrath's role and mission as 1st Platoon Commander with 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marines in Afghanistan?
real_qa.r: Brian was 1st Platoon Commander for Fox Company, 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marines, deployed to southern Helmand Province from October 2009 to May 2010. His platoon's mission was counterinsurgency: going village to village, setting up mini patrol bases, clearing Taliban, and then introducing USAID and other agencies to help with farming and development. His platoon was the southernmost unit and tip of the sword for the battalion, pushing toward the Afghanistan-Pakistan border.

real_qa.q: How did Brian McGrath transition from Marine Corps officer to construction laborer and then to senior project leadership?
real_qa.r: After leaving active duty in 2010, Brian's father-in-law offered him a position in construction and got him into Laborers Union Local 57, heavy highway division in Philadelphia. He started as a laborer on projects for University of Pennsylvania, Thomas Jefferson University, and GlaxoSmithKline, learning to read drawings and understand construction fundamentals. He then transitioned into estimating before his father-in-law became ill, at which point he met Joey Fay, a Marine lieutenant colonel at Quattrofoil, and joined that firm.
real_qa.requete: Marine Corps to construction transition laborer to project leader

real_qa.q: What was Peace Lambs Grade School project and what was its budget and timeline at MCFA?
real_qa.r: Peace Lambs Grade School was Brian's first project at Quattrofoil, a collaboration between Wexford Science and Technology, Drexel University, and the School District of Philadelphia located in University City Philadelphia. The project had a two-year timeline and a budget of twenty-nine million dollars, and was managed by general contractor BSI Construction.
real_qa.requete: Peace Lambs Grade School Philadelphia budget timeline

real_qa.q: What key leadership principle does Brian McGrath emphasize when working with architects, engineers, and contractors on construction projects?
real_qa.r: Brian emphasizes listening and respecting expertise rather than asserting authority over specialists he doesn't have expertise in. He states he is not the expert on engineering, architecture, or interior design, so he listens to their input, provides detailed feedback, and maintains honest accountability rather than simply dismissing their recommendations. He believes this collaborative listening approach makes success much better for all stakeholders involved in the project.
real_qa.requete: construction project team leadership listening collaboration

guest.bio_context: Brian McGrath served as a platoon commander with the 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marines in southern Afghanistan from October 2009 to May 2010, executing counterinsurgency operations in Helmand Province. After leaving active duty, he started in construction as a laborer in the Laborers Union Local 57, then progressed through estimating at his father-in-law's contracting company before joining Quattrofoil (now MCFA) two years ago. He is currently pursuing an MBA while managing a diversified portfolio of commercial, residential, and institutional projects.
